description: switch this repo's event log to per-run drop files and rewrite its docs

spec_impact_justification: Repository setting for the framework's own event log and its documentation; no requirement text changes.

description: events layout follow-up: guide pointer and stale docstrings
summary: docs/guide.md now points to the per-run event layout section; two test docstrings no longer call the layout dormant.
spec_impact_justification: Documentation and docstrings only; no requirement text changes.
none_reason: User guide paragraph and two test docstrings; no requirement or behaviour changes.

description: iterate prose and verifier hint are layout-neutral
summary: The iterate skill references and the finalization verifier message now cover both the single-file and the per-run event layout.
spec_impact_justification: Wording only; the verifier's pass/fail logic is unchanged.

affected_acs.why: new criterion: strict external review signal and partial marker

description: External review: reviews_expected/missing_legs, opt-in require_all_legs/--min-reviews strictness, partial marker in the review state (issue #1035)
events writer hardening, round 2: one name rule, order across a rotation, torn-file append
summary: One drop-file name rule shared by writer, reader, staging, fold and integrity check; first event of a new file orders after the run key's earlier events; a torn file is never appended to.
spec_impact_justification: FR-01.11 already promises ordered, uncorrupted per-run event files; this makes the code keep that promise, no new promise.

description: External review: opt-in ordered gpt_leg.routes list that falls through when a route is unavailable or fails at runtime and records every attempt (issue #1034)
summary: The GPT reviewer can now be given an ordered list of routes (codex, openrouter, direct) and moves on to the next one when a route is missing or fails, instead of ending without a review.

affected_acs.why: new criterion: ordered GPT-leg route list with runtime fall-through and recorded attempts

description: events fold at release: changelog Step 5.3 folds old per-run event files in its own commit, never blocks the release
summary: New tools/fold_events_for_release.py (stage + commit exactly the touched paths, rollback on any failure, open_files in every report) called by the changelog skill before the release is staged.
spec_impact_justification: Release tooling for housekeeping the docs already ask for (fold now and then, as single-actor release work); no new promise to a user.

description: events open-file warning, A7 wording, adopt seeder LF
summary: main_health and F0 now warn when 150 or more event files are open, the adopt check names both event locations, and the adopt seeder writes plain line endings on Windows.
spec_impact_justification: Advisory operator hint and wording; the events layout behavior itself is unchanged.

description: U1 tag binding: lexer-based suite brace depth, unbound covers warning, untagged-modified text
summary: Test tags on suites are now scoped correctly even when the code contains brace characters in strings or comments, a requirement comment that binds nothing is reported as a warning, and the untagged-modified stop names both ways out.

affected_acs.why: new AC minted for this change; fixtures in test_suite_tags_lexer.py and gate/audit tests

description: verifier and release-notes scripts declare their own packages
summary: The finalization verifier and the release-notes tools now carry their own package list, so a plain uv run works from any folder without hand-added packages.
spec_impact_justification: Tooling start-up only; no product behavior changes.

description: triage consistency: G4 closing-token audit, project-root either side, status-less append reads as triage
summary: The compliance audit now notices a commit that says it closes a triage card while the card is still open, the triage CLI accepts the project folder before or after the command, and an item with a damaged status shows up as open instead of vanishing.
spec_impact_justification: Internal audit and reader tolerance; no requirement text changes.
none_reason: audit check, CLI argument parsing and reader tolerance in plugins/ and shared/ tooling

description: audit G2: judge each part of a comma-joined commit scope; remove the false promise of an automatic skip
summary: The compliance audit now checks each part of a commit scope such as daemon,lib on its own and names only the unknown part, and its text no longer claims adopted projects are skipped automatically; it points to the two explicit ways out.
spec_impact_justification: Audit tooling and its text; no requirement text changes.
none_reason: audit check scope parsing and audit documentation under plugins/ and docs/

description: Decode git/gh output as UTF-8 bytes in pr_review_local and check_required_checks; verifier text names the unrecoverable late-record case
summary: On Windows the local PR-review diff and the required-checks drift detector no longer garble non-ASCII text or turn a lone carriage return into a line break.
spec_impact_justification: Restores the already specified drift-detection behaviour on Windows; no promise changes.

description: leadwright follow-up bundle: G2 whole-string match, G4 detail ids, honest G4 test tags, bloat extraction, one-line describe lexer leak
summary: Five small follow-ups from the leadwright campaign: G2 keeps matching comma stoplist entries, G4 lists open card ids, the G4 test is tagged at FR level, one audit file is back under 300 lines, and a one-line describe no longer leaks its tag.
spec_impact_justification: Audit and collector hardening; no requirement text changes.
none_reason: audit checks and tag collector under plugins/shipwright-compliance

description: origin-aware finding dedup + curried test declarations
summary: The sync that files GitHub findings no longer creates duplicate cards when a checkout is behind origin, and tests written as it.skipIf(cond)(title) are now counted.

AC42 already counts a data-driven declaration as one test; curried skipIf/runIf declarations now follow the same rule.
